title: First Unique Character
contract: Return the index of the first character appearing once in a lowercase string, or −1.
brute: for(int i=0;i<s.length();i++){int count=0;for(int j=0;j<s.length();j++)if(s.charAt(i)==s.charAt(j))count++;emit("Count one character across the string","index",i,"count",count);if(count==1)return i;}return -1;
optimal: int[] count=new int[26];for(char c:s.toCharArray())count[c-'a']++;for(int i=0;i<s.length();i++){emit("Find the first frequency-one position","index",i,"count",count[s.charAt(i)-'a']);if(count[s.charAt(i)-'a']==1)return i;}return -1;
reasoning: Count a candidate throughout the string before deciding whether it is unique.
Build all counts once, then make a second ordered pass.
The second pass must follow input order, not hash iteration order, because the required result is the earliest index.
